references: Tolerance and failure injections are authored protocol cases, not recordings from a vendor process. Native ACP and Orch companion support are distinguished explicitly.

approval_checkpoint.reason: Command checkpoints are another program’s control protocol; DSH has one-shot tool permission requests.

approval_mcp.reason: Native DSH ACP exposes MCP tool calls but no separate MCP approval request family.

approval_network.reason: The native server does not emit a network-specific approval; unknown tool requests still receive a generic card.

approval_permissions.reason: Native ACP exposes tool permission requests, not a separate permissions-details request kind.

approval_plan.reason: Native DSH ACP intentionally omits presentation plans; the Orch companion supplies plan review.

approval_prompt_user_rule.reason: Native DSH offers one-shot allow/reject choices and does not offer durable prompt-user rules.

background_end.reason: Native ACP has no background-End control. Orch executor-backed commands and companion extras retain their existing End tests.

background_wake.reason: Native ACP has no background-wake control; Orch owns the continuation and executor-backed command lifecycle.

compaction_automatic.reason: The published native ACP server does not report a compaction cause. Automatic versus manual cannot be inferred from a generic update.

compaction_idle.reason: Native DSH ACP does not emit an idle compaction update in this release; no turn or duration is invented.

compaction_manual.reason: Native DSH ACP has no manual compaction control. The Orch companion reports compaction phases.

compaction_marker.reason: This release’s native DSH ACP updates do not emit a completed compaction marker. Companion phase behavior remains separately tested.

fork.reason: The published native DSH ACP server explicitly does not provide fork. Orch companion fork is a separate extension, covered by dsh-bridge session tests.

hooks.reason: Native DSH ACP omits UI-specific hook notifications. A future native method is still counted, never silently dropped.

mcp_elicitation.reason: The native server intentionally omits elicitation. Generic unknown permission requests remain cancellable.

mcp_failure.reason: Native DSH ACP does not publish a separate MCP startup-failure notification; ordinary failed tools retain their actual status.

mcp_startup.reason: Native DSH ACP does not publish MCP startup status; the actual mounted MCP tool call is covered.

model_reroute.reason: DSH pins a prompt’s selected model at admission and has no native reroute notification. Native configuration reports are covered without relabelling an old model call.

steer.reason: Native ACP has no steering method; this is an Orch companion extension, covered by the existing plugin/control tests.

usage_limit.reason: DSH ACP has no subscription-plan limit facts. Raw provider failures are retained, but a plan/reset fact cannot be invented.

user_input.reason: Native DSH ACP intentionally omits elicitation and interactive questions; Orch companion questions use its own native request path.
